models.name: familiar_surprisal_graded_costly_l3
models.rationale: Pragmatic listener at depth 3 with perceptual isolation, feature surprisal, graded semantics, utterance costs, and familiarization.

models.name: familiar_surprisal_graded_costly_l4
models.rationale: Pragmatic listener at depth 4 with perceptual isolation, feature surprisal, graded semantics, utterance costs, and familiarization. Refines surprisal_isolated_graded_costly_l4 by incorporating familiarization base-rate sensitivity from familiar_isolated_graded_costly_l2 into the shared referent prior. Listeners reason at depth 4, inverting a speaker who anticipates a depth-3 pragmatic listener's interpretation. Visual pop-out is determined by an object's perceptual isolation (nearest-neighbor contrast), candidate referents are prioritized by cumulative contextual feature surprisal and prior familiarization base rates, semantic applicability diminishes with additional competing features (graded truth), and speakers evaluate communicative utility trade-offs with utterance extension costs. On uninformative prior trials, choices follow the integrated isolation, surprisal, and familiarization prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

models.name: rsa_l2 (seed)
models.rationale: RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2, uniform prior over objects. One more level of recursion than the vanilla model: a speaker S2 chooses words by how well the depth-1 pragmatic listener L1 would recover the object (exp(alpha * log L1)), and the listener L2 inverts S2. Depth-2 reasoning is what the pragmods "complex" game needs to single out the object described by the twice-implicated word. One rationality alpha at every level; uniform choice with no informative word; a lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

metric.lede: How well each model predicts which referent people pick in the held-out conditions: conditions of the same papers that the loop never saw. Every model was fitted to the loop's training trials only. The panels show people's choice proportions against the models' predictions for each held-out game, word and condition.
metric.standing_note: Held-out log predictive density behind the best of these models, in nats (whiskers ±2 SE of the difference, clustered by held-out condition). Lower is better. r and RMSE compare predicted and observed choice proportions over held-out display cells.
